source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Both palms flat and open, fingers pressed together pointing straight upward (Anjali Mudra).
startPos: In front of mid-chest, fingertips level with upper chest / chin.
palmOrientation: Palms pressed firmly against each other, thumbs near the sternum.
movementDirection: Hold steady at chest center, with a slight polite head nod.
instructions: Bring both open hands in front of your chest.
Press your palms and fingers together flat, pointing straight up.
Hold hands centered at heart level and nod slightly to express greeting and respect.
avoid: Do not separate the palms or keep fingers wide apart.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary / INCLUDE Dataset
handshape: Open flat palm, fingers together or naturally relaxed.
startPos: Beside the temple / ear at head height.
palmOrientation: Palm facing outward toward the observer / camera.
movementDirection: Wave side-to-side gently 2 to 3 times, or touch temple and move outward.
instructions: Raise your dominant hand to ear / temple height.
Face your open palm directly toward the camera.
Perform a crisp, clear wave side to side or outward from the temple.
avoid: Do not hide your fingers or wave outside the webcam field of view.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary / INCLUDE Dataset
handshape: Flat open dominant hand touching chin, then supporting non-dominant hand.
startPos: Dominant fingertips touch chin, left hand near waist.
palmOrientation: Dominant palm faces inward toward face, then forward.
movementDirection: Move hand forward from chin ('Good'), then raise dominant forearm upward like the rising sun ('Morning').
instructions: Touch the fingertips of your dominant hand to your chin and bring it forward for 'Good'.
Place your left hand under your right elbow as a horizon line.
Raise your right forearm upward smoothly to represent the sun rising in the morning.
avoid: Keep both arms clearly inside the frame during the rising motion.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary / INCLUDE Dataset
handshape: Dominant flat hand touching chin, then lowering over horizontal base arm.
startPos: Fingertips at chin ('Good'), non-dominant forearm horizontal.
palmOrientation: Palm faces downward toward the base arm.
movementDirection: Forward from chin, then arch dominant forearm gently downward like the setting sun.
instructions: Sign 'Good' by touching your chin with flat fingertips and moving forward.
Hold your non-dominant arm horizontally in front of you.
Curve your dominant forearm downward toward the horizontal arm to signify evening.
avoid: Do not drop hands below the bottom edge of the webcam.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Open hand with fingers together, curling inward together rhythmically.
movementDirection: Open and gently bend four fingers downward toward palm 2 times.
instructions: Raise your dominant hand to chest or shoulder height.
Face your palm toward the person you are communicating with.
Gently bend and open your fingers in the standard farewell gesture.
avoid: Do not wave erratically; keep the motion controlled.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary / INCLUDE Dataset
handshape: Both hands open, palms facing upward, slightly cupped.
startPos: Held at mid-chest height, palms facing up, about 15 cm apart.
movementDirection: Tilt hands gently forward and outward in a questioning arc.
instructions: Bring both hands in front of your mid-chest with open palms facing upward.
Move both hands slightly forward and tilt outward with an inquisitive facial expression.
Hold the open pose momentarily for the model to confirm.
avoid: Keep both hands within camera view; do not flip palms downward.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Thumbs-up or open hand touching chest lightly, moving into confident OK gesture.
palmOrientation: Thumb pointing straight up, fingers closed into fist.
movementDirection: Firm downward or forward confirmation nod with the hand.
instructions: Form a confident thumbs-up sign at chest level.
Move the hand slightly forward and nod your head in confirmation.
Express reassurance through a relaxed, positive posture.
avoid: Do not obscure the thumb with other fingers.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Point toward other person ('You'), 'H' or index tap on chest ('Name'), open palms ('What').
palmOrientation: Index finger forward, then two fingers tapped together, then palms up.
movementDirection: Sequential ISL phrase: YOU + NAME + WHAT.
instructions: First point index finger forward toward the person ('You').
Touch index and middle finger of dominant hand to the other hand across chest ('Name').
Turn both palms upward with raised eyebrows ('What?').
avoid: Do not rush; perform each sign clearly in sequence.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Flat hand on chest ('My'), followed by two fingers crossed / tapped ('Name'), then finger-spelling.
startPos: Open flat palm touching center of your chest.
movementDirection: Tap chest ('My'), sign 'Name', then spell initial letters using ISL finger alphabet.
instructions: Touch your own chest with an open flat palm ('My').
Tap your index and middle fingers together to sign 'Name'.
Follow with your ISL finger-spelled name.
avoid: Keep finger spelling at shoulder height.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Circular rubbing on chest ('Pleased / Good'), then both index fingers coming together ('Meet').
startPos: Right hand on chest, then both hands with index fingers extended pointing upward.
palmOrientation: Palms facing each other during the meet phase.
movementDirection: Rub chest circle, then bring index fingers together until knuckles touch.
instructions: Place open palm on chest and rub clockwise once ('Pleased / Good').
Raise both hands with index fingers extended pointing upward.
Bring both index fingers together until they touch, signifying two people meeting.
avoid: Ensure index fingers touch in the center of the camera frame.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Closed fist with thumb rested against fingers, knuckles facing forward.
startPos: In front of chest / shoulder height.
movementDirection: Nod the entire fist up and down from the wrist 2 times like a head nodding yes.
instructions: Make a loose fist with your dominant hand at chest height.
Face your knuckles forward toward the webcam.
Bend your wrist up and down twice in a crisp nodding motion.
avoid: Do not move the whole arm; the nod should come cleanly from the wrist.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Index and middle fingers extended together with thumb extended; fingers snap shut against thumb, or index finger wags side-to-side.
movementDirection: Snap index and middle finger tips quickly onto the thumb tip, or shake index finger side-to-side.
instructions: Extend your index and middle fingers together, with thumb pointing outward.
Snap the index and middle fingertips quickly down onto your thumb.
Accompany with a gentle head shake to convey negative agreement.
avoid: Do not keep pinky or ring fingers extended.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Open flat palm, fingers together.
startPos: Resting flat against the center of your chest.
movementDirection: Rub in a smooth circular motion on the chest 2 to 3 times clockwise.
instructions: Place your open flat hand against the center of your chest.
Keep fingers straight and held together.
Move your hand in a gentle circular clockwise rubbing motion over your heart.
avoid: Do not lift palm away from chest during the circle.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary / INCLUDE Dataset
handshape: Flat open hand, fingers straight and pressed together.
startPos: Fingertips lightly touching your chin or lower lip.
movementDirection: Move the hand smoothly forward and slightly downward toward the camera.
instructions: Touch the tips of your flat fingers to your chin or lips.
Move the hand straight forward in a smooth extending gesture toward the other person.
Keep your palm angled slightly upward as you finish the forward motion.
avoid: Do not wave side-to-side; the motion is direct and forward.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Fist with thumb across fingers ('A' handshape).
palmOrientation: Knuckles facing outward, thumb side against chest.
movementDirection: Rub in a small circular motion on the chest.
instructions: Make a closed fist with your dominant hand.
Place your fist flat against the center of your chest.
Rub in small circular motions while adopting an apologetic facial expression.
avoid: Keep fist on the chest; do not swing your elbow wildly.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Open flat hands, palms facing up, curved inward.
startPos: Extended slightly outward to the sides.
movementDirection: Sweep both hands inward toward your body in an inviting gesture.
instructions: Hold both open hands slightly outward in front of you with palms facing up.
Sweep both hands inward smoothly toward your chest to welcome the guest.
Accompany with a warm, welcoming smile.
avoid: Do not drop hands below camera view.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Open palm held upright facing forward, fingers spread slightly.
startPos: Chest to shoulder height, arm bent.
movementDirection: Hold steady, with subtle finger flexion or gentle downward pulse.
instructions: Raise your dominant hand with palm facing outward toward the camera.
Keep fingers pointing straight up.
Hold steady for 1 second to signal 'Wait / Hold on'.
avoid: Do not tilt palm sideways.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Firm vertical open flat palm pushed forward, or dominant flat hand brought down sharply on open non-dominant palm.
movementDirection: Decisive forward push or sharp chop down onto non-dominant palm.
instructions: Raise your dominant hand with palm facing outward toward the camera.
Push hand forward firmly and hold still to signal an immediate stop.
Alternatively, bring your dominant hand edge down firmly onto your open left palm.
avoid: Do not wave; the gesture is abrupt and authoritative.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Open hand with palm facing inward or downward, fingers waving inward toward body.
startPos: Extended forward in front of chest.
movementDirection: Curl fingers inward toward your chest repeatedly.
instructions: Extend your hand forward at chest height with palm facing inward or down.
Curl your fingers repeatedly toward yourself to beckon the person.
Keep motion smooth and polite.
avoid: Do not gesture aggressively.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Cupped hand or index finger pointing to ear.
palmOrientation: Cupped palm behind ear, or index tapping earlobe.
movementDirection: Hold cupped hand behind ear or tap earlobe 2 times.
instructions: Bring your dominant hand up to the side of your ear.
Cup your hand slightly behind the ear or tap your ear with your index finger.
Look toward the speaker to show active listening.
avoid: Do not cover your ear completely.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Non-dominant flat open palm facing upward; dominant hand forms a thumbs-up fist resting on top.
startPos: Held together at lower chest height.
palmOrientation: Left palm facing up; right fist resting on left palm.
movementDirection: Lift both hands together upward and inward toward yourself.
instructions: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of your chest with palm facing upward.
Place your dominant hand in a thumbs-up shape directly on top of the open palm.
Lift both hands together upward toward your chest to ask for help.
avoid: Keep both hands joined together as they lift.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Dominant hand cupped like holding a glass, or 'W' handshape tapping chin.
movementDirection: Tilt cupped hand toward mouth like drinking water.
instructions: Cup your dominant hand as if holding a small glass of water.
Bring it up to your mouth and tilt your hand slightly as if drinking.
Optionally point to yourself to emphasize 'I need'.
avoid: Do not block your face completely from camera view.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: All fingertips brought together into a point ('eating' mudra) and brought toward mouth, or flat hand rubbing stomach.
startPos: Fingertips together in front of chest.
movementDirection: Touch fingertips toward mouth 2 times, then rub stomach.
instructions: Bring all five fingertips of your dominant hand together in the traditional Indian food/eating gesture.
Move them toward your lips twice ('Eat/Food').
Rub your stomach gently to indicate hunger.
avoid: Ensure hand does not obscure the webcam view.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Index finger extended.
startPos: Tip of index finger touching throat / Adam's apple.
movementDirection: Trace index finger down your throat from neck to clavicle.
instructions: Place your index finger at the top of your throat.
Draw it downward in a straight line to signify dryness in the throat.
Follow with the drinking gesture to communicate thirst clearly.
avoid: Keep your neck and upper chest visible in camera.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Bent hands with fingertips resting on chest / shoulders.
startPos: Fingertips resting lightly on upper chest near shoulders.
movementDirection: Allow wrists and elbows to drop downward while shoulders slump.
instructions: Touch the fingertips of both curved hands to your upper chest.
Drop your hands and wrists downward heavily in a release of energy.
Let your shoulders drop slightly to mirror fatigue.
avoid: Do not let hands drop completely out of view.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Open flat left hand supporting thumbs-up right fist, pulled inward toward self.
movementDirection: Lift both hands together toward your chest urgently.
instructions: Place your thumbs-up right hand upon your flat open left hand.
Draw both hands firmly toward your chest.
Use an urgent facial expression to convey the need for assistance.
avoid: Keep fists steady on the base palm.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Both index fingers extended pointing toward each other.
startPos: Near the area of pain, or in front of chest.
palmOrientation: Index tips pointing directly toward each other without touching.
movementDirection: Jab index fingers toward each other with a twisting, sharp pulse.
instructions: Extend both index fingers pointing toward each other ~10 cm apart.
Twist and jab them inward toward each other sharply.
Winced facial expression communicates pain intensity.
avoid: Keep the twist crisp and centered in frame.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Index and middle fingers of right hand tapping inside of left wrist (checking pulse), followed by telephone hand at ear.
palmOrientation: Left palm facing up; right fingers tapping pulse.
movementDirection: Tap wrist pulse 2 times, then raise 'phone' hand (thumb and pinky extended) to ear.
instructions: Hold left wrist forward with palm facing up.
Tap the inside of your left wrist with two fingers of your right hand as if feeling a pulse ('Doctor').
Hold thumb and pinky out to your ear ('Call / Telephone').
avoid: Keep both the wrist tap and phone sign visible in sequence.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: 'E' handshape or open hands waving rapidly back and forth in front of chest.
movementDirection: Rapid urgent shaking back and forth to indicate crisis.
instructions: Raise both hands to chest height with an alert posture.
Shake hands urgently back and forth while signaling distress.
Direct attention to the emergency situation immediately.
avoid: Do not sign calmly; speed and urgency are key.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Thumb and pinky extended ('telephone' shape), placed at ear, then gesturing outward.
movementDirection: Hold phone shape at ear, then point outward to ask someone to dial.
instructions: Form the telephone sign with your thumb at your ear and pinky near your mouth.
Point toward the other person or phone with an appealing expression.
Sign 'Please' by rubbing chest if time permits.
avoid: Make sure the hand shape is recognizable.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Open flat hands, palms facing chest.
movementDirection: Brush upward against chest repeatedly in gentle fluttering strokes.
instructions: Place both open hands in front of your chest with palms facing your body.
Brush your hands upward in buoyant repeated motions.
Pair with a wide, genuine smile to reflect the emotion.
avoid: Do not brush downward; happy signs always move upward.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Open curved hands, fingers slightly spread.
movementDirection: Draw hands slowly downward in front of face like tears or a heavy heart.
instructions: Hold both open hands in front of your face with palms facing inward.
Slowly draw them downward past your chin while tilting your head slightly down.
Adopt a somber, sad facial expression.
avoid: Keep the downward motion slow and deliberate.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Open hands spreading rapidly from fists in front of chest.
movementDirection: Open hands suddenly with trembling or shivering motion.
instructions: Hold both fists in front of your chest.
Snap them open suddenly with trembling fingers as if startled.
Pull hands back slightly toward your body in recoil.
avoid: Facial expression is essential: wide eyes and open mouth.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Clawed hand with bent, tense fingers.
startPos: In front of stomach / lower chest.
movementDirection: Pull clawed hand sharply upward toward chest/neck as if rage is boiling up.
instructions: Form a tense claw shape with your dominant hand.
Start at your stomach and pull the claw sharply upward toward your chest.
Furrow your eyebrows and clench your jaw to convey anger.
avoid: Do not keep fingers limp or relaxed.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Thumb, index finger, and pinky finger extended; middle and ring fingers folded into palm (🤟).
movementDirection: Hold steady in front of you, or push slightly forward with affection.
instructions: Extend your thumb, index finger, and pinky finger upright simultaneously.
Fold your middle and ring fingers flat against your palm.
Hold your hand steady facing the webcam at shoulder height.
avoid: Do not bend the pinky or index finger; all three extended digits must be straight.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Index finger flicks upward near temple, followed by head shake.
movementDirection: Flick index finger upward off thumb, then shake head.
instructions: Place your index finger near your forehead.
Flick the finger upward and shake your head from side to side.
Express a puzzled look on your face.
avoid: Make the head shake clear to distinguish from 'I understand'.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Fist with index finger flicking up near temple, followed by affirmative head nod.
movementDirection: Flick index finger upright like a lightbulb turning on, then nod.
instructions: Hold a loose fist near your temple.
Flick your index finger straight up as if an idea just appeared.
Nod your head affirmatively to confirm understanding.
avoid: Do not shake your head.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Both hands open, palms facing up, thumbs and fingers wiggling or pinching in question.
movementDirection: Bend and wiggle fingers rhythmically with questioning eyebrows.
instructions: Hold both hands in front of your mid-chest with palms facing up.
Wiggle your fingers or pinch your index and thumb rhythmically.
Raise your eyebrows in a friendly inquiring question.
avoid: Keep both hands centered inside the frame.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Index finger pointing forward and moving away ('Go'), then open palms facing up ('Where?').
palmOrientation: Index pointing forward, then palms up.
movementDirection: Arc index finger forward away from body, then tilt open palms side to side.
instructions: Point your dominant index finger forward and move it away from your body ('Go').
Turn both open hands palms-up and tilt them side-to-side ('Where?').
Look in the direction of the inquiry.
avoid: Keep movement fluid between the two components.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Both hands open, fingertips touching at an angle forming a roof shape ('Home').
palmOrientation: Palms angled toward each other, fingertips touching like a roof.
movementDirection: Form the roof shape of a house, then gesture forward to go.
instructions: Touch the fingertips of both hands together at an angle to create the roof of a house ('Home').
Hold the roof shape firmly in center frame.
Move hand forward to indicate 'Want to go'.
avoid: Do not let palms collapse flat against each other; maintain the peaked roof.

hindi: क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकते हैं?
source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Thumbs-up right hand on open flat left hand, lifted inward with questioning facial expression.
palmOrientation: Left palm facing up; right fist on top.
movementDirection: Lift both hands together inward toward chest with raised eyebrows.
instructions: Place your thumbs-up dominant hand onto your flat open base palm.
Lift both hands toward yourself while raising your eyebrows inquiringly.
Hold briefly for recognition.
avoid: Keep hands steady and centered.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Right hand bent at right angle, arcing over and landing into left open palm ('Again / Repeat').
startPos: Left hand open flat; right hand poised above.
palmOrientation: Left palm up; right palm facing left.
movementDirection: Arc right hand up and down firmly into center of left palm.
instructions: Hold your non-dominant hand flat with palm facing up.
Curve your dominant hand and bring it down into the open palm repeatedly ('Again / Repeat').
Polite expression signals request to repeat.
avoid: Ensure the landing into the palm is visible.

english: I need to use the bathroom
source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: 'T' handshape (thumb tucked between index and middle fingers) shaken side to side, or little finger held up.
movementDirection: Shake 'T' handshape side to side gently.
instructions: Form a fist with your thumb poking out between your index and middle fingers ('T' for toilet).
Shake your hand gently side to side at shoulder height.
Alternatively, hold pinky finger extended (common Indian classroom sign for restroom).
avoid: Keep hand clearly in view of camera.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: OK handshape (index and thumb forming a circle, other three fingers upright) or thumbs-up.
startPos: In front of chest / shoulder height.
movementDirection: Hold the OK sign steady or give a reassuring nod.
instructions: Join the tips of your thumb and index finger into a circle.
Keep your middle, ring, and pinky fingers spread upright.
Hold the sign facing the camera with a reassuring smile.
avoid: Do not let the other three fingers collapse into your palm.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Cap visor / brim shape: Index and thumb curved near forehead temple.
startPos: Dominant hand at forehead / temple height.
palmOrientation: Palm facing downward / inward towards temple.
movementDirection: Hold near temple like gripping the brim of a cap (traditional sign for Boy).
instructions: Raise dominant hand to forehead / temple level.
Touch or hold index and thumb near the temple like touching a cap visor.
Hold steady for visual recognition.
avoid: Do not drop hand below chin height.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Index finger extended, other fingers gently curled.
startPos: Index fingertip touching cheek or tracing jawline (referencing earring).
movementDirection: Touch or trace index fingertip along the cheek or earlobe.
instructions: Extend index finger while folding remaining fingers.
Touch or trace index finger along your cheek or near earlobe.
Hold clearly beside face for camera detection.
avoid: Do not block your face or mouth from the camera.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Index finger pointing straight UP, other fingers curled into palm.
movementDirection: Hold steady.
instructions: Extend your index finger straight up.
Keep thumb and other three fingers closed into your palm.
Hold upright at chest height.
avoid: Do not extend the middle finger.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Index and Middle fingers UP in a V shape.
movementDirection: Hold steady.
instructions: Extend your index and middle fingers upward in a clear V shape.
Keep ring and pinky fingers curled tightly with thumb.
Hold in front of camera.
avoid: Do not hide either finger behind the other.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Thumb extended outward, Index and Middle fingers UP.
movementDirection: Hold steady.
instructions: Extend thumb outward and raise index and middle fingers.
Keep ring and pinky fingers folded into palm.
Hold upright in camera.
avoid: Do not curl thumb back in.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Four fingers (Index, Middle, Ring, Pinky) UP, thumb tucked into palm.
movementDirection: Hold steady.
instructions: Extend all four fingers (index, middle, ring, pinky) straight up.
Tuck thumb across palm.
Hold steady at chest level.
avoid: Do not extend thumb.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: All five fingers extended and spread open.
movementDirection: Hold steady.
instructions: Open all five fingers wide and spread at chest level.
Face palm directly toward the camera.
Hold steady for instant counting translation.
avoid: Do not raise to ear level (which means Hello).

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Pinky finger extended UP only, other four fingers curled.
movementDirection: Hold steady.
instructions: Raise only your pinky finger straight up.
Fold index, middle, ring, and thumb into a fist.
Hold upright clearly.
avoid: Do not let index finger rise.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Thumb OUT and Index UP forming an L shape.
movementDirection: Hold steady.
instructions: Extend index finger upward and thumb outward to form an L shape.
Fold other three fingers into palm.
Hold steady at chest level.
avoid: Do not raise middle finger.

source: ISLRTC Official Indian Sign Language Dictionary
handshape: Both open hands showing 5 + 5 spread fingers.
palmOrientation: Both palms facing outward toward camera.
movementDirection: Hold steady side-by-side.
instructions: Raise both hands at chest level.
Open all fingers on both hands (5 + 5 = 10).
Hold clearly in camera view.
avoid: Do not overlap hands.
